subject: MOVE statement
notes: kb/Work PB370 (w1102f, w1107a): CONFORMS, with two defects of GR1's intermediate fixed. (1) ORDER: the sender's evaluation precedes the receivers' (identifier-1 'evaluated only once, immediately before data is moved to the first of the receiving operands'); a store keeps it through PlaceIdentification.SenderFirst (kb/Work PB3261), and a receiver's pre-op (a function-bearing subscript) is ordered after the sender's freeze, which SendingValueTemp.Positioned places where the sender finished binding, at N = 1 (when such a pre-op exists) and N > 1 alike. (2) DIGITS: the numeric function-identifier's temporary had the fixed 30-digit scale-9 description, so MOVE FUNCTION PI TO S1 S2 into PIC 9V9(12) stored 3.141592653000 where MOVE FUNCTION PI TO S1 stores 3.141592653589, and a 25-digit NUMVAL value lost its four high-order digits; the equivalence 'MOVE a TO temp / MOVE temp TO b' was not exact. SendingValueTemp.IntermediatePic, the one description of the intermediate (merged with kb/Work PB3268, which describes it for the value and its use), sizes it: a binary64 value takes a binary64 item; a set of floating-point items of one binary format takes that format; the widest floating-point edited item +9.9(35)E+9999 for a floating-point set holding an edited receiver; exactly the receivers' widest digits for an all-fixed-point set (SendingValueTemp.ShapedPic); and, where those digits pass the 38-digit carrier (PIC 9(31) beside PIC V9(28), branch review R3-1: the capped scale cut MOVE FUNCTION NUMVAL ('1234567890123456789012.123456789') TO X Y's Y to seven fraction digits), the 36-digit floating-point edited item for a non-integer value. The documented limits are a mixed set and that beyond-the-carrier set for a binary64 value (docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-92). Witnesses conformance:cases/14.9.25-MOVE/pb370_move_function_value_digits and conformance:cases/14.9.25-MOVE/pb370_move_first_condition. || kb/Work PB394 + PB886 + PB896 (wave 42) - EVERY SENTENCE OF GR1 NOW CONFORMS, and the three that were open were three different failures of the SAME intermediate. (1) 'evaluated only once' for a reference modifier / subscript / function-identifier landed 2026-09-13 over SendingValueTemp. (2) 'The length of the data item referenced by identifier-1 is evaluated only once' for a GROUP sender whose extent is decided at run time: SendingValueTemp.FreezeOdoExtent gives the cloned intermediate a controller temp holding data-name-1's value at the hoist with the clone's OccursSpec.Depending pointed at it, inside CreateCompilerTemp because DataItem.OccursSpec is init-only. Measured at 2023: MOVE 3 TO N / MOVE ODO-G TO N, Z now gives N=1 Z=[125  ] where it gave Z=[1    ]; the JUSTIFIED form gives [  125] (13.18.38.4 GR8 a)'s current extent, right-aligned by 13.18.34.4 GR1); DEPENDING INSIDE the group gives Y=[3125    ]. (3) The intermediate's CARRIER: RefModPlace.PositionCount replaces ImageWidth, because 8.4.3.3.4 GR5 a) fixes the UNIT of the count ('If the usage of identifier-1 is bit, positions used in evaluation are bit positions; otherwise, positions used in evaluation are character positions') while ImageWidth is an OCCUPANCY in characters - a PIC 1(8) USAGE BIT item occupies ONE character and counts EIGHT positions, and a DYNAMIC LENGTH item occupies none statically. MOVE BE(1:4) TO B1 B2 now gives [1011][1011] where it gave [1000][1000]; the national and dynamic-length siblings of the same sweep are measured right. (4) GR1's ZERO-LENGTH-ITEM clause now reaches the GROUP shapes: 8.5.4's stem ('whose minimum length is zero') is implemented as ONE recurrence, DataItem.MinimumLengthIsZero, rather than four copies of its group bullets, and MoveEmitter's zero-length arm puts the statement's own store in its else branch because GR1's substitution changes the move's KIND (GR4's first sentence makes the substituted-literal move ELEMENTARY). Measured: MOVE ZG TO a PIC 9(3) receiver with a zero-occurrence occurs-depending group gave 000 and now gives spaces - the same answer as the MOVE "" TO the same receiver that GR1 says it is AS IF. Which of 8.5.4's group shapes is REACHABLE is 14.9.25.3 SR9's business: items 5 and 7 are variable-length groups, refused against a non-group receiver at compile time (COBOL1931, witnessed by conformance:cases/14.9.25-MOVE/pb896-variable-length-group-to-elementary), so item 1 is the shape that gets here and the predicate covers the rest without a second site. retired-witness: conformance:85/pb896_zero_length_group_sender (the golden moved to the 2014 corpus: it writes a zero-length literal, a COBOL-2014 introduction gated by kb/Work PB895 (same program, same expected output)) retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/ReceivingReach.cs#Of (kb/Work PB3268's finisher merged PB370's ReceivingReach into PB3268's one intermediate description, SendingValueTemp.IntermediatePic / ShapedPic; ReturnedValuePicFor and ReceivingReach are deleted) retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/SendingValueTemp.cs#ReturnedValuePicFor (kb/Work PB3268's finisher merged PB370's ReceivingReach into PB3268's one intermediate description, SendingValueTemp.IntermediatePic / ShapedPic; ReturnedValuePicFor and ReceivingReach are deleted)
